title: API reference
text:
API reference

The current API reference for the Codly package.

- [Components](components/index.md) render code blocks and their parts.
- [Types](types/index.md) describe configuration values and their accepted shorthand forms.
- [Themes and helpers](helpers/index.md) apply reusable styles and inspect block metadata.

 Imports

Import the Codly package as a namespace:

typst
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly


 Components and styling

> [!TIP] Style components with show rules.
> Use show: codly.number-set_(...) to set defaults in scope.
> The -show_ helpers accept replacement content or a callback receiving
> the component, rather than a dictionary of field overrides.

Codly uses Elembic custom elements and types. [codly.new](components/new.md) creates a code block. Component helpers such as [codly.number-set_](components/number.mdsignature) apply defaults within the surrounding Typst scope. They are used with show:, rather than native set syntax. Refer to the [elembic documentation](https://pgbiel.github.io/elembic/) for more information.

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.number-set_(numbering: "1.")
show raw.where(block: true): codly.new
py
print(42)
print(43)



Each component page documents its constructor and available -set_ and -show_ helpers. Many configuration types do not render content directly, instead being meant to be called internally by Codly. Most values can be built from dictionaries or arrays instead of needing manual type invocation. Whether the elements/types can be shown and their constructors are detailed on their respective pages.

 Coordinates and defaults

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> Source-line ranges are one-indexed and inclusive. Character highlights
> use zero-indexed offsets with an exclusive end. Displayed line numbers
> can change with offsets and skipped lines.

Source-line ranges are one-based and include both endpoints. Character highlights use zero-based bounds with an exclusive end; callout pointers and explicit skip positions have their own conventions documented on their type pages. Displayed line numbers can differ from source positions after applying an offset. Check the field's definition before using displayed numbers as configuration coordinates.

auto and none have field-specific meanings. A default value does not always describe the final appearance: themes, scoped styling rules, and surrounding Typst text or raw settings can affect rendering.

paint means a color, gradient, or tiling. array  means an array of values of type T. The type notation in signature blocks describes accepted values; it is not runnable Typst syntax. The preview examples are runnable and editable.

> [!WARNING] Signatures describe types.
> Signature blocks show the accepted argument types; they are not runnable
> Typst examples. Use the preview examples as a starting point for your code.

title: new
text:
codly.new

Creates a formatted code block. [codly.new](signature) is an alias of [codly.codly](signature); [codly.set_](behavior), [codly.show_](behavior), and [codly.selector](behavior) target the same element.

 Signature

typst code
codly.new(body, ..fields)


body is positional and required. It accepts source text, a path, or content containing raw blocks. Other fields are named. The setters accept named field values; show_ installs a scoped replacement callback, and selector creates a Typst selector for block instances.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | none \| str \| path \| content | Required | Raw source text, a caller-resolved file path, or content. |
| file | auto \| none \| str \| path \| content | auto | Filename badge; auto uses the input path basename and none hides it. |
| lang | auto \| none \| str | auto | Language for source or path input; auto infers from the file extension. |
| lang-position | auto \| none \| alignment | auto | Language badge placement. Top/bottom place it in header/footer; left/right alone reserves space by the first code row. |
| file-position | none \| alignment | top + left | Filename badge placement; none hides it. |
| block-label | auto \| none \| label | auto | auto uses the nearest enclosing figure's label; an unlabeled inner figure stops discovery. none disables block references; a label sets the target explicitly. |
| alias | none \| str | none | Marks a block as already aliased. |
| number-enabled | none \| bool | true | Whether the automatic line-number column is shown. |
| diff | auto \| none \| bool \| diff | auto | Diff processing; false or none disables it, while true or a diff configuration enables it. |
| gutters | auto \| array  | auto | Ordered columns before code. auto keeps the ordinary number column; an empty array hides all gutters. |
| offset | int \| label \| auto | 0 | Added to source line numbers; a label continues numbering and auto renumbers the first selected line to 1. |
| range | none \| range | none | Source-line range to display. |
| ranges | none \| array  | none | Multiple source-line ranges to display. |
| smart-skip | none \| bool \| smart-skip | false | Controls collapsed skipped lines. |
| aliases | none \| dictionary | (:) | Language aliases. |
| smart-indent | none \| bool | true | Enables indentation-aware wrapping. |
| wrap-marker | none \| content | none | Symbol shown on wrapped continuation lines when smart indentation is enabled. |
| skip-last-empty | none \| bool | true | Whether to omit a final empty source line. |
| breakable | none \| bool | true | Whether the block can break across pages. |
| skips | none \| array  | none | Explicit skipped-line configuration. |
| skip-line | none \| content \| array  | align(center)[ ... ] | Content used for skipped source lines. |
| skip-number | none \| content \| array  | [ ... ] | Content used for skipped line numbers. |
| unnumbered | none \| array  | () | Source lines to display without a line number. |
| annotations | none \| array  | none | Annotations beside source-line ranges. |
| callouts | none \| array  | none | Callouts attached to source positions. |
| highlighted | none \| array  | () | Whole-line highlights. |
| highlights | none \| array  | none | Highlight regions and palettes. |
| header | none \| content | none | Content above the code. |
| footer | none \| content | none | Content below the code. |
| radius | none \| length | 0.32em | Corner radius of the block. |
| padding | length \| dictionary | 0pt | Extra inner edge space, separate from row inset and leading. A dictionary may use top, right, bottom, left, x, y, and rest. |
| leading | none \| length | none | Vertical space between rows. |
| gutter | none \| length | none | General spacing between grid rows and columns. |
| column-gutter | none \| length | none | Horizontal spacing between block columns. |
| row-gutter | none \| length | none | Vertical spacing between block rows. |
| sublangs | none \| array  | none | Languages applied to inclusive source-line ranges. |
| rainbow | none \| bool \| rainbow | none | Opt-in syntax-aware delimiter colors. |
| indent-guides | none \| bool \| indent-guides | none | Opt-in indentation guides. |
| width | length \| ratio \| auto | 100% | Block width; auto fits natural width up to the available width. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Figure labels are discovered automatically.
> Label the enclosing figure once. Codly discovers that label automatically,
> so omit the block-label argument from codly.new.

> [!WARNING] Unlabeled inner figures stop discovery.
> A code block inside an unlabeled nested figure does not inherit an outer
> figure's label. Label the inner figure to enable references to its code.

> [!WARNING] Sublang blocks performance may be impacted.
> Sublang blocks may degrade performance, due to the requirement of re-parsing and leveraging introspection for each sublang block.

Fields are validated and cast by their declared types. Gutter arrays and functions cast to gutter-column; gutters: auto includes the ordinary number column when enabled, and custom columns remain when number-enabled is false. Custom gutters replace diff's automatic old/new/marker columns. Diff colors may be paints, none, auto (the ordinary row fill), or callbacks receiving a row with diff information. Explicit highlights take precedence over diff backgrounds.

Ranges select source lines before display. Diff references count displayed patch rows; highlight and callout character positions count code characters without diff markers. Diff context uses new-side syntax, and each hunk or file is highlighted independently.

show: codly.set_(..fields) sets named field defaults in scope. show: codly.show_(it => content) replaces matching blocks with the callback result; return it inside the result to retain the block. show codly.selector(): it => content uses a native Typst selector. selector accepts outline, outer, and meta boolean options, all defaulting to false; these select Elembic representation layers rather than filtering fields.

 Example

yaml widgets
- type: select
  name: example-language
  label: Language
  default: '"python"'
  options:
    - label: Python
      value: '"python"'
    - label: Rust
      value: '"rust"'


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

set raw(lang: example-language)

codly.new(
  
  def greet(name):
      print(f'Hello, {name}!')
  ,
  file: "greeting.py",
  offset: 10,
)


 Example: Automatic Code Blocks
typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show raw.where(block: true): codly.new

py
def greet(name):
    print(f'Hello, {name}!')

title: lang
text:
codly.lang

Creates the language badge used by a Codly code block, with language definitions and badge styling.

 Signature

typst code
// Define a language badge for a Codly code block.
codly.lang(
  body: str,
  languages: dictionary | none = (:),
  default-color: paint | none = rgb("283593"),
  inset: length | dictionary | none = 0.32em,
  outset: dictionary | none = (x: 0.32em, y: 0em),
  radius: length | dictionary | none = 0.32em,
  stroke: stroke | function | none = (lang) => lang.color + 0.5pt,
  fill: paint | function | none = (lang) => lang.color.lighten(80%),
  display-name: bool | none = true,
  display-icon: bool | none = true,
  align: alignment | none = right + horizon,
)

// Equivalent set-rule for a language badge.
codly.lang-set_(..args)

// Override the show-rule for a language badge.
codly.lang-show_(it, ..args)


body is the required positional language key (for example, "py"). All other fields are named. [codly.lang-set_(..args)](signature) sets defaults for language badges in its scope; [codly.lang-show_(it => ...)](signature) installs a show rule that receives each badge element and returns replacement content. These helpers use the same field names as the element.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | str | Required, positional | Language key matched against languages. |
| languages | dictionary \| none | (:) | Map from language keys to definitions; see [codly.language](../types/language.md). |
| default-color | paint \| none | rgb("283593") | Color used when the matching definition has no color. |
| inset | length \| dictionary \| none | 0.32em | Inner padding around the badge contents. |
| outset | dictionary \| none | (x: 0.32em, y: 0em) | Placement offset used with the badge. |
| radius | length \| dictionary \| none | 0.32em | Corner radius of the badge. |
| stroke | stroke \| function \| none | (lang) => lang.color + 0.5pt | Badge border; a function receives (name: ..., icon: ..., color: ...). |
| fill | paint \| function \| none | (lang) => lang.color.lighten(80%) | Badge background; a function receives (name: ..., icon: ..., color: ...). |
| display-name | bool \| none | true | Whether to show the configured name, or the raw key when no definition exists. |
| display-icon | bool \| none | true | Whether to show the configured icon. |
| align | alignment \| none | right + horizon | Alignment used when Codly places the badge. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Unknown language keys stay visible.
> If languages has no matching entry, the badge shows the raw language key
> and uses default-color. Add a definition when you want a display name or
> icon.

The languages dictionary maps raw language tags to [codly.language](../types/language.md) values. Its values also accept a string as shorthand for a displayed name, or a dictionary. A missing entry displays the raw key and uses default-color; a matching entry supplies its name, optional icon, and optional color.

Language definitions can preserve extra fields. For a matching key, display-name, display-icon, fill, stroke, inset, and radius in that definition override the corresponding badge fields. The definition's color is used by fill and stroke callbacks through their lang dictionary; outset, align, and default-color are not per-language overrides.

If both name and icon are hidden or unavailable, the badge renders no content. Setting fill or stroke to none removes that decoration.

 Example: Typical Usage

> [!NOTE] This is an example for configuring
> In practice, you would style the language badge according to your needs, but you would not instantiate it directly. 

yaml widgets
- type: slider
  name: badge-radius
  label: Badge radius
  default: 4pt
  unit: pt
  min: 0
  max: 12
  step: 1


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.lang-set_(
  radius: badge-radius,
  languages: (
    py: (name: [Python], color: rgb("3476a8"), icon: "🐍"),
  ),
)

codly.lang(
  "py",
  inset: 5pt,
)


 Example: Custom Renderer

> [!NOTE] This is an example for configuring
> In practice, you would style the language badge according to your needs, but you would not instantiate it directly. 

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly
import "@preview/elembic:1.1.1" as e

show: codly.lang-set_(languages: (
  py: (name: [Python], color: rgb("3476a8"), icon: "🐍"),
))

show: codly.lang-show_(it => {
  // Get the fields through elembic
  let fields = e.fields(it)

  // Get the language definition
  let lang = fields.languages.at(fields.body, default: none)
  if lang == none {
    return none
  }

  // Make a custom badge
  box(
    fill: lang.color.lighten(80%),
    stroke: 1pt + lang.color,
    outset: 0pt,
    inset: 2pt,
    [ lang.name - lang.icon ],
  )
})

codly.new(py
def main():
    print("Hello, Python!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
)

title: file
text:
codly.file

Creates the filename badge used beside a code block or in its header or footer.

 Signature

typst code
// Create a filename badge
codly.file(
  body: str | content,
  fill: paint | none = luma(240),
  stroke: stroke | none = 0.5pt + luma(160),
  inset: length | dictionary = (x: 0.4em, y: 0.2em),
  radius: length | dictionary = 2pt,
)

// Equivalent set-rule for codly.file
codly.file-set_(..args)

// Equivalent show rule for codly.file
codly.file-show_(it => ...)


body is required and may be supplied positionally; it is the displayed filename or filename content. The remaining fields are named. [codly.new](new.md) documents how code blocks derive and place this badge.

[codly.file-set_(..args)](signature) sets badge defaults in its scope using the fields below. [codly.file-show_(it => ...)](signature) installs a show rule that receives each file badge element and returns replacement content; it does not take field overrides.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | str \| content | Required, positional | Displayed filename. |
| fill | paint \| none | luma(240) | Badge background; none removes the fill. |
| stroke | stroke \| none | 0.5pt + luma(160) | Badge border; none removes the border. |
| inset | length \| dictionary | (x: 0.4em, y: 0.2em) | Inner padding around the filename. A length applies uniformly; a dictionary can set axes independently. |
| radius | length \| dictionary | 2pt | Corner radius. A length applies uniformly; a dictionary can set corners individually. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Pass a path to codly.new
> When the code input is a path, [codly.new](new.md) reads the file, derives the badge text from its basename, and uses its extension as the language when lang is omitted. Set file or lang explicitly to override those defaults.

The badge is a box using fill, stroke, inset, and radius around body. The fields are validated against their declared types; inset and radius accept either one length or a dictionary. file-set_ applies element defaults in the surrounding scope, and file-show_ replaces the rendered badge through its callback.

 Example

yaml widgets
- type: slider
  name: example-radius
  label: Corner radius
  default: 4pt
  unit: pt
  min: 0
  max: 12
  step: 1
- type: select
  name: fill
  label: Badge fill
  default: 'rgb("d8eaff")'
  options:
    - label: Pale blue
      value: 'rgb("d8eaff")'
    - label: Pale green
      value: 'rgb("d9f5df")'
    - label: No fill
      value: 'none'


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.file("src/main.typ", radius: example-radius, fill: fill)

title: header
text:
codly.header

Creates a configurable header element for a Codly code block.

 Signature

typst code
// Create a header element
codly.header(
  body,
  repeat: false,
  align: center + horizon,
  inset: auto,
  fill: luma(240),
  stroke: auto
)

// Equivalent set-rule for codly.header
codly.header-set_(..fields)

// Equivalent show rule for codly.header
codly.header-show_(it => ...)


body is required and positional; all other fields are named.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content \| none | Required, positional | Content displayed in the header. |
| repeat | bool \| none | false | Repeat the header on later pages when the block breaks across pages. |
| align | alignment \| none | center + horizon | Alignment of the header content in its cell. |
| inset | length \| dictionary \| auto \| none | auto | Space around the header content; auto leaves the grid-cell default in effect. |
| fill | paint \| auto \| none | luma(240) | Header cell background. none leaves it unfilled; auto uses the default header fill. |
| stroke | stroke \| auto \| none | auto | Stroke around the header cell; auto leaves the grid-cell default in effect. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Put the filename badge in the header
> codly.new places its file badge in the header by default. Supplying a custom header body keeps the badge alongside that body; style the badge separately with [codly.file-set_(...)](file.md).

The required body is positional, and the remaining fields are named. When used by [codly.new](new.md), the header cell spans the code block's columns. repeat controls the underlying grid header's repetition. Setting fill to auto resolves to luma(240); the header fill is independent of line and number fills. The block's outer corner radius is configured on [codly.new](new.md), not on the header element.

[codly.header-set_(..fields)](signature) sets defaults for matching headers in scope. [codly.header-show_(replacement)](signature) installs a scoped replacement callback or content replacement for matching headers. A callback receives the header element as it, not a dictionary of field overrides.

 Example

yaml widgets
- type: select
  name: example-fill
  label: Header fill
  default: 'rgb("d8eaff")'
  options:
    - label: Pale blue
      value: 'rgb("d8eaff")'
    - label: Pale green
      value: 'rgb("d9f5df")'
    - label: No fill
      value: 'none'
- type: slider
  name: example-radius
  label: Block corner radius
  default: 4pt
  unit: pt
  min: 0
  max: 12
  step: 1


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  py
  print('hello')
  ,
  header: codly.header([Greeting · Python], fill: example-fill, inset: 5pt),
  radius: example-radius,
)

title: footer
text:
codly.footer

Creates the footer element rendered below a [code block](new.md).

 Signature

typst code
// Create a footer element
codly.footer(
  body,
  repeat: false,
  align: center + horizon,
  inset: auto,
  fill: none,
  stroke: auto
)

// Equivalent set-rule for codly.footer
codly.footer-set_(..args)

// Equivalent show rule for codly.footer
codly.footer-show_(it => ...)


body is required and positional; all other fields are named.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content \| none | required | Footer content. |
| repeat | bool \| none | false | Repeat the footer on each page when the code block spans pages. |
| align | alignment \| none | center + horizon | Alignment of the footer content in its cell. |
| inset | length \| dictionary \| auto \| none | auto | Inset around the footer content. |
| fill | paint \| auto \| none | none | Footer cell background. none leaves it unfilled; auto uses the footer's default. This fill is independent of line and number fills. |
| stroke | stroke \| auto \| none | auto | Stroke around the footer cell. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Footer fill defaults to none
> fill: auto resolves to the footer's default (none). Set an explicit fill when the footer should have a background; its fill is independent of line and number fills.

Pass this element as the footer field of [codly.new](new.md). Plain footer content is also accepted there and is wrapped as a footer with its defaults. A [codly.footer-set_(...)](signature) rule supplies defaults, while fields set on an explicit [codly.footer(...)](signature) take precedence. The repeat field controls whether the footer appears on continuation pages.

[codly.footer-show_(callback)](signature) applies a show rule to footer elements. The callback receives the element and must return replacement content; for example, show: codly.footer-show_(it => [it]) preserves the footer body. These wrappers follow Typst's scoped set and show rules.

 Example

The footer fill can be changed while previewing:

yaml widgets
- type: select
  name: footer-fill
  label: Footer fill
  default: luma(240)
  options:
    - label: Light gray
      value: 'luma(240)'
    - label: Pale blue
      value: 'rgb("e8f0ff")'
    - label: None
      value: 'none'

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  js
  const ready = true;
  ,
  footer: codly.footer([Generated output], fill: footer-fill, inset: 5pt),
)

title: line
text:
codly.line

A generated row component that styles one displayed line in a Codly code block. Codly creates these rows while rendering [codly.new](new.md); use the set/show wrappers here to configure their style.

 Signature

typst code
codly.line(body, ..fields)


body is required and positional. All other fields are named and optional.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content \| none | Required | Content displayed in the row. |
| radius | length \| none | 0.32em | Corner radius for the row styling. |
| inset | length \| dictionary \| none | 0.32em | Row padding; a dictionary accepts directional inset values. |
| fill | auto \| paint \| array  \| function \| none | (luma(240), none) | Row background. A paint or none applies to every body row; an array cycles by displayed-row index; a function receives the row dictionary described below. auto restores the default palette. |
| stroke | stroke \| none | 1pt + luma(240) | Border around the row. |
| highlights | array  \| none | none | Character-level highlights for this row; see [codly.highlight-config](../types/highlight-config.md). |
| smart-indent | bool | true | Continue wrapped rows at their original indentation. |
| block-label | label \| none | none | Label of the containing code block. |
| reference | dictionary \| none | none | Internal reference details for an unnumbered source line. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Callback indexes include generated rows.
> The index passed to a fill callback counts displayed rows from zero,
> including header and footer rows; those rows themselves do not invoke the
> callback.

> [!TIP] Whole-line highlights win.
> A row's highlight fill takes precedence over the fill selected by this
> element, so use highlight styling when a highlighted line needs a distinct
> background.

The fill callback receives a dictionary with index, kind, source-line, and number. index is zero-based in displayed-row order, including a header or footer if present. kind is "code", "skip", or "callout" for callback rows. source-line is the one-based source line for code and callout rows, and none for generated skip rows. number is the displayed line number, or none for unnumbered and generated rows. Header and footer rows count toward the index but do not invoke this callback. Whole-line highlights take precedence over this fill.

[codly.line-set_(..args)](signature) sets row fields with show:, while [codly.line-show_(it => ...)](signature) replaces or wraps each generated row through a show rule. The show wrapper receives the row content as it, not a dictionary of field overrides.

 Example

The slider changes the fill selected for code rows; the attached callout uses a separate fill.

yaml widgets
- type: slider
  name: row-green
  label: Code-row green channel
  default: 224
  min: 0
  max: 255
  step: 1


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.line-set_(fill: row => {
  if row.kind == "callout" { purple.lighten(80%) }
  else if row.kind == "code" { rgb(255, row-green, 190) }
  else { luma(238) }
})

codly.new(
  py
  let answer = 42
  print(answer)
  ,
  callouts: ((line: 1, body: [The value is set here.]),),
)

title: number
text:
codly.number

A displayed line number in a Codly code block; number-set_ configures its style and number-show_ replaces its rendered content.

 Signature

typst code
codly.number(number, parent, ..fields)


number and parent are required positional fields; the remaining fields are named. Codly normally creates these elements while rendering [codly.new](new.md).

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| number | none \| content \| int \| array  | Required | Value to display; none suppresses it. |
| parent | any | Required | Parent content of the line. |
| numbering | str \| function | numbering.with("1") | Numbering pattern or callback used for integer values. |
| align | alignment \| none | left + horizon | Alignment of the number in its cell. |
| placement | "inside" \| "outside" \| none | "inside" | Whether the number column sits inside or outside the code block. |
| fill | auto \| paint \| none | auto | Number-cell background; auto follows the corresponding code row's fill. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Custom content bypasses numbering.
> A content value is rendered as-is, while integer values go through
> numbering. Use an integer when you want the configured numbering style to
> apply.

An integer is formatted with numbering; an integer array is passed as multiple numbering values. A content value is displayed directly, and number: none displays nothing. Numbering functions receive the integer value, or the array's values as separate arguments. number-set_(..fields) sets scoped fields with show:. number-show_(it => ...) receives the number element as it and replaces it; it does not receive a dictionary of field overrides.

The placement setting applies to the number column for code blocks in scope. Outside placement also positions any configured gutters outside the code.

 Example

The switch moves the rendered line-number column outside the code block.

yaml widgets
- type: switch
  name: number-outside
  label: Place numbers outside
  default: false


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

title: highlight
text:
codly.highlight

[codly.highlight](signature) renders a styled span over part of a source line in a Codly code block.

 Signature

typst code
codly.highlight(body, highlight: highlight-config | none = none)
codly.highlight-set_(..args)
codly.highlight-show_(it, ..args)


 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content \| none | Required, positional | Highlighted span content. |
| highlight | highlight-config \| none | none | Span metadata supplied by Codly, including source positions and local overrides; see [codly.highlight-config](../types/highlight-config.md). |
| color | paint \| array  | Thesis theme's five-color highlight palette | Base paint or cycling palette for highlights. The palette must not be empty. |
| radius | length \| none | 0.32em | Corner radius of the highlight box. |
| fill | function \| none | color => color.lighten(80%) | Transforms the selected highlight paint into the box fill. |
| baseline | length \| auto \| none | 0pt | Baseline shift for the highlight box; auto follows the content baseline. |
| stroke | stroke \| function \| none | color => 0.5pt + color | Box stroke, or a callback that derives it from the selected paint. |
| inset | length \| dictionary \| none | 0.32em | Space between the highlighted content and box edges. A dictionary uses Typst inset sides. |
| outset | length \| dictionary \| none | 0em | Space the highlight box extends outside its layout bounds. |
| clip | bool \| none | true | Whether the highlight box clips its content. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] References need a labelled figure.
> To use references to highlights, by using label to identify them, you must ensure that the Codly code block is contained within a labelled figure. 

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> Highlight line numbers are one-indexed. Character offsets are zero-indexed,
> and end is exclusive.

> [!WARNING]
> A highlight palette must contain at least one color. An empty array causes
> a compilation error.

Codly emits this element for spans declared in a code block's highlights field. Span positions are zero-indexed character offsets, with an exclusive end; line numbers are one-indexed. Bounds must be nonnegative; omitted or none bounds start at the beginning or extend through the end of the line. See [codly.highlight-config](../types/highlight-config.md) for span metadata fields.

Each code block has an independent highlight-paint cycle, separate from whole-line highlighting. A scalar color repeats for every span; an array cycles in declaration order. An explicit paint in the span metadata uses that paint without advancing the cycle, while its callback receives the next palette paint. The element's fill and stroke callbacks receive that resolved span paint. Per-span radius, clip, inset, outset, baseline, and stroke settings override the corresponding element fields when present.

[codly.highlight-set_(..args)](signature) sets fields for matching highlight elements in the current scope. [codly.highlight-show_(it, ..args)](signature) installs replacement content or a callback that receives the highlight element. Both follow Typst's scoped show-rule behavior.

 Example

yaml widgets
- type: slider
  name: example-radius
  label: Corner radius
  default: 4pt
  unit: pt
  min: 0
  max: 12
  step: 1

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.highlight-set_(radius: example-radius)

codly.new(
  py
  let answer = 42
  ,
  highlights: ((line: 1, start: 4, end: 10),),
)

title: annotation
text:
codly.annotation

[codly.annotation](signature) is the generated brace element displayed beside an annotated source-line range in a Codly code block.

 Signature

typst code
// Create a new annotation.
codly.annotation(body, ..fields)

// Equivalent set-rule for an annotation.
codly.annotation-set_(..args)

// Override the show-rule for an annotation.
codly.annotation-show_(it, ..args)


Codly creates this element while rendering [codly.new](new.md); its fields describe the rendered brace and are usually supplied by Codly. body is the required positional content field. The remaining fields are named.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content \| none | Required, positional | Content attached to the annotation; none leaves only its number. |
| label | content \| none | Required; declared default: "todo" | Hidden reference-anchor content associated with a labelled annotation. Codly supplies this field. |
| height | length \| none | 0pt | Height of the brace spanning the rendered rows. |
| num | int \| none | 0 | Automatically assigned annotation number. |
| numbering | function \| none | numbering.with("(1)") | Formats num; use none to hide the number. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] References need a labelled figure.
> To use references to annotations, by using label to identify them, you must ensure that the Codly code block is contained within a labelled figure. 

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> Annotation line numbers are one-indexed. And end line is inclusive.

Codly emits one annotation element for a configured line range. Range endpoints are one-indexed source-line positions, independent of displayed line-number offsets; annotation ranges cannot overlap. Use [codly.annotation-config](../types/annotation-config.md) to configure a range.

[codly.annotation-set_(..args)](signature) sets fields on generated annotation elements in the current scope. [codly.annotation-show_(it, ..args)](signature) installs replacement content or a callback receiving the generated element. The callback can inspect its fields, including body, height, num, and numbering; it does not receive a dictionary of field overrides.

 Example: Basic Usage

yaml widgets
- type: switch
  name: show-annotation-number
  label: Show annotation number
  default: true

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  py
  prepare()
  result = compute()
  print(result)
  cleanup()
  ,
  annotations: ((
    start: 2,
    end: 4,
    content: [Computes and displays the result],
    numbering: if show-annotation-number { n => [(n)] } else { none },
  ),),
)

title: bubble
text:
codly.bubble

A pointed callout bubble rendered next to a source line, with independent defaults for its paint, dimensions, spacing, and pointer.

 Signature

typst code
// A codly pointed callout bubble.
codly.bubble(
  body,
  gap: 0.5em,
  pointer-align: "center",
  pointer-size: 0.4em,
  pointer-height: auto,
  pointer-width: auto,
  pointer-offset: 0pt,
  align: center,
  fill: luma(245),
  stroke: 0.6pt + luma(80),
  inset: (x: 0.5em, y: 0.3em),
  outset: 0pt,
  radius: 2pt,
  width: auto,
  line: int,
  pointer: int,
  placement: "below"
)


[codly.bubble](signature) is the generated element type for pointed callouts. Its body is positional; line and pointer are required named fields when representing the element directly. In normal use, create bubbles by setting pointer on a callouts entry.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content | required, positional | Content displayed inside the bubble. |
| gap | length \| dictionary | 0.5em | Minimum separation from neighboring bubbles; a length applies on both axes, or use (x: ..., y: ...). |
| pointer-align | "start" \| "center" \| "end" | "center" | Preferred alignment of the bubble around its source character; placement clamps it to the row. |
| pointer-size | length | 0.4em | Default pointer height and half its base width. |
| pointer-height | length \| auto | auto | Pointer height; auto uses pointer-size. |
| pointer-width | length \| auto | auto | Full pointer base width; auto uses twice pointer-size. |
| pointer-offset | length | 0pt | Horizontal shift of the pointer tip from its source character; positive is right, negative is left, and the tip is clamped to the bubble. |
| align | alignment | center | Alignment of the bubble content. |
| fill | paint \| none | luma(245) | Fill shared by the bubble and pointer. |
| stroke | stroke \| none | 0.6pt + luma(80) | The bubble's single outline, including its pointer. |
| inset | length \| dictionary | (x: 0.5em, y: 0.3em) | Padding inside the bubble. |
| outset | length \| dictionary | 0pt | Extra paint extent around the body; reserved in the row. |
| radius | length | 2pt | Bubble corner radius. |
| width | length \| ratio \| auto | auto | Preferred padded body width; auto fits content, bounded by the available row. |
| line | int | required, named | One-indexed source line attached to the bubble. |
| pointer | int | required, named | Source character anchor, one-indexed, with 0 at the start of the line. |
| placement | "above" \| "below" | "below" | Side of the source line on which to place the bubble. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Bubbles can share a row
> Consecutive bubbles on the same side of a source line share a row when their outlines fit. If they collide, Codly places them in separate lanes in declaration order; adjust gap or width to control the spacing and wrapping.

The bubble and arrow use one outline and fill. Content wraps at the available width. Negative dimensions, pointer sizes, insets, and outsets are rejected. Styling defaults set on [codly.bubble](signature) are inherited by generated bubbles; explicit [codly.callout](callout.md) settings and then entry-level bubble settings take precedence. A callout with pointer: none does not produce a bubble.

 Rules

[codly.bubble-set_(..args)](signature) sets styling defaults for generated bubbles. Use it for the style fields above.

[codly.bubble-show_(it, ..args)](signature) installs a show rule for generated bubbles. Its first argument is a replacement callback or content, not a dictionary of field overrides.

 Example: Basic Usage

yaml widgets
- type: slider
  name: pointer
  label: Pointer position
  default: 17
  min: 0
  max: 26
  step: 1

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.bubble-set_(fill: aqua.lighten(75%), radius: 6pt, width: 125pt)
codly.new(
  js
  let total = subtotal + tax
  ,
  callouts: ((
    line: 1,
    pointer: pointer,
    body: [The final amount includes tax.],
  ),),
)


 Example: Custom Show Rule
typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.bubble-show_(it => {
  box(stroke: red, it)
})

codly.new(
  js
  let total = subtotal + tax
  ,
  callouts: ((
    line: 1,
    pointer: 17,
    body: [The final amount includes tax.],
  ),),
)

title: callout
text:
codly.callout

A row attached to a source line in a Codly code block; it can be plain text or a pointed bubble.

 Signature

typst code
// Create a new callout.
codly.callout(
  body,
  line: int,
  align: auto,
  breakable: auto,
  inset: auto,
  fill: auto,
  stroke: auto,
  source-indent: false,
  placement: "below",

  // Parameters for the bubble if any.
  bubble-gap: auto,
  bubble-align: auto,
  bubble-fill: auto,
  bubble-stroke: auto,
  bubble-inset: auto,
  bubble-outset: auto,
  bubble-radius: auto,
  bubble-width: auto,
  
  // Parameters for the bubble's pointer if used.
  pointer: none,
  pointer-align: auto,
  pointer-size: auto,
  pointer-height: auto,
  pointer-width: auto,
  pointer-offset: auto,
)


body is positional. line is required and named. Normally, callouts are created by entries in the callouts field; see [codly.callout-config](../types/callout-config.md).

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content | required, positional | Content displayed in the row or bubble. |
| line | int | required, named | One-indexed source line to attach to. |
| align | alignment \| auto \| none | auto | Alignment of the callout cell; auto inherits the code block's cell alignment. |
| breakable | bool \| auto \| none | auto | Whether the callout cell may break across pages; pointed bubble groups stay together. |
| inset | length \| dictionary \| auto \| none | auto | Inset of the callout cell. |
| fill | paint \| auto \| none | auto | Fill of the callout cell. |
| stroke | stroke \| auto \| none | auto | Stroke of the callout cell. |
| source-indent | bool | false | Aligns a plain callout with source indentation while reserving gutter columns; pointed bubbles remain character-anchored. |
| placement | "above" \| "below" | "below" | Side of the attached source line. |
| bubble-gap | length \| dictionary \| auto | auto | Minimum separation between bubbles; use a length for both axes or (x: ..., y: ...). |
| pointer-offset | length \| auto | auto | Horizontal shift of the tip from the source character; positive is right, negative is left, and the tip is clamped to the bubble. |
| bubble-align | alignment \| auto | auto | Bubble content alignment, independent of the cell alignment. |
| bubble-fill | paint \| none \| auto | auto | Fill shared by the bubble and arrow. |
| bubble-stroke | stroke \| none \| auto | auto | Single outline shared by the bubble and arrow. |
| bubble-inset | length \| dictionary \| auto | auto | Padding inside the bubble. |
| bubble-outset | length \| dictionary \| auto | auto | Extra paint extent around the bubble body, reserved in the row. |
| bubble-radius | length \| auto | auto | Bubble corner radius. |
| bubble-width | length \| ratio \| auto | auto | Preferred padded body width; auto fits content within the available row. |
| pointer | int \| none | none | Character anchor in the source line: one-based, with 0 at line start. Set to none for a plain row. |
| pointer-align | "start" \| "center" \| "end" \| auto | auto | Preferred bubble alignment around the anchor; placement clamps it to the available row. |
| pointer-size | length \| auto | auto | Arrow height and half of its base width. |
| pointer-height | length \| auto | auto | Arrow height; auto uses pointer-size. |
| pointer-width | length \| auto | auto | Full arrow base width; auto uses twice pointer-size. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Plain callouts can follow source indentation
> Set source-indent: true to align a plain callout with the source indentation while preserving the gutter columns. Pointed callouts stay anchored to their source character.

Callout lines are source-line coordinates, unaffected by displayed line-number offsets. Pointer positions count characters in the source line, with zero denoting its start; the pointer follows the rendered character when code wraps. Negative pointers, dimensions, insets, outsets, and gaps are rejected. A bubble's body and arrow share one fill and outline, and bubble text wraps to its available width.

Unspecified or auto bubble styling inherits from [codly.bubble](bubble.md), after explicit [codly.callout](signature) styling. Entry values in callouts take precedence over the element's set-rule values. Explicit none disables bubble fill or stroke; pointer: none keeps a callout plain.

[codly.callout-set_(..args)](signature) sets defaults for callout cells and bubbles. [codly.callout-show_(it, ..args)](signature) installs a show rule; its first argument is replacement content or a callback, such as it => [it], not a dictionary of field overrides. Bubble-specific defaults and show rules are documented on [codly.bubble](bubble.md).

 Example

yaml widgets
- type: switch
  name: source-indent
  label: Align plain callout to source indentation
  default: true


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.callout-set_(source-indent: source-indent)
codly.new(
  py
  if ready:
    start()
  ,
  callouts: (
    (line: 1, body: [Plain callout aligned with the source.]),
    (line: 2, pointer: 3, body: [Pointing at start.]),
  ),
)

title: ref
text:
codly.ref

> [!WARNING] References need a labelled figure.
> To use references to highlight, lines, or annotations, you must ensure that the Codly code block is contained within a labelled figure. 

Sets shared formatting for references to code lines, highlights, and annotations.

 Signature

typst code
codly.ref(body, by: "line", sep: "-", numbering: numbering.with("1"))
codly.ref-set_(..fields)


[codly.ref](signature) is an element definition. Use [codly.ref-set_(...)](signature) to set its fields in the current scope; it is a set-rule wrapper, not a separate element. There is no ref-show_ wrapper because references use Typst's native reference syntax and the generated reference elements' show rules.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content \| none | required | Content of the reference element. |
| by | "line" \| "item" \| none | "line" | Choose a displayed line number or an item label/content for highlight and annotation references. |
| sep | str \| content \| none | "-" | Content between the native reference to the code block and the line number or item. |
| numbering | function \| none | numbering.with("1") | Formats line numbers when by is "line"; none leaves the native block reference without a line suffix. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Choose what the reference shows.
> The shared by: "line" setting shows the displayed line number. by: "item" shows the highlight tag or annotation content instead.

> [!WARNING] Item references to highlights need a tag.
> When by: "item", each referenced highlight must define a tag; Codly reports an error if the tag is missing. Annotation item references use the annotation's content.

The fields in [codly.ref](signature) are shared defaults for [codly.line-ref](line-ref.md), [codly.highlight-ref](highlight-ref.md), and [codly.annotation-ref](annotation-ref.md). A field set directly on one of those generated reference elements takes precedence over the shared setting. by: "item" uses the highlight's tag or the annotation's content; line references always refer to a displayed line. Numbering callbacks receive the displayed line number. These references resolve to the containing code figure or block, so ordinary Typst reference formatting still applies to that target.

See [codly.line-ref](line-ref.md), [codly.highlight-ref](highlight-ref.md), and [codly.annotation-ref](annotation-ref.md) for the generated reference fields.

 Example

This figure labels a code block and an annotation. The reference to the annotation uses its content as the item suffix:

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.ref-set_(by: "item", sep: " — ")

figure(caption: [A code example])[
  codly.new(
    
    first line
    second line
    ,
    annotations: ((start: 2, label:  , content: [the note]),),
  )
] 

The annotation reference is @note and the line is @example:2.

title: line-ref
text:
codly.line-ref

> [!WARNING] References need a labelled figure.
> Put the code block inside a labelled figure to enable line references.
> Codly detects that figure label automatically, so omit the block-label
> argument from codly.new.

Formats native Typst references to displayed lines in labeled Codly code blocks.

 Signature

typst code
codly.line-ref(body, block: label, number: int, suffix: none, separator: auto, numbering: auto)
codly.line-ref-set_(..args)
codly.line-ref-show_(it, ..args)


[codly.line-ref](signature) is a generated element definition; Codly creates it for line targets, so user code normally refers to those targets with @block:line rather than constructing the element. line-ref-set_(...) applies field defaults to generated line references in the current scope. line-ref-show_(it) installs a show rule; its first argument is the replacement callback or content, not field overrides.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content \| none | required | Internal reference body supplied by Typst. |
| block | label | required, named | Label of the containing code block. |
| number | int | required, named | Displayed line number. |
| suffix | content \| none | none | Optional suffix attached to the displayed line number. |
| separator | auto \| str \| content \| none | auto | Content between the native block reference and line number; auto uses [codly.ref](ref.md) settings. |
| numbering | auto \| function \| none | auto | Formats the displayed line number; auto uses [codly.ref](ref.md) settings, while none leaves only the native block reference. |

 Behavior

The constructor is exported, but references are normally generated from native reference syntax. The element has no custom casts and cannot itself carry a label. Its fields are checked against the declared types; block and number are named required fields on the generated element. Codly generates line targets for labeled blocks, and @block:line references the block figure followed by the line formatter. The number is the displayed line number, including the block's numbering behavior, rather than a character position in the source.

separator: auto and numbering: auto inherit [codly.ref](ref.md)'s sep and numbering settings. Explicit fields set through line-ref-set_ override those shared defaults for line references in scope. A numbering function receives the displayed line number. line-ref-show_ lets a show rule replace or wrap the generated reference; its callback receives the element.

See [codly.ref](ref.md) for shared reference defaults.

 Example

This self-contained example labels a code block and refers to its second displayed line. The local set rule changes the separator and line-number format:

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.line-ref-set_(separator: " line ", numbering: n => [Ln])

figure(caption: [A small code block])[
  codly.new(
    
    first line
    second line
    ,
  )
] 

The reference points to line two of the block: @example:2.

title: highlight-ref
text:
codly.highlight-ref

> [!WARNING] References need a labelled figure.
> To use references to highlight, you must ensure that the Codly code block is contained within a labelled figure. 

[codly.highlight-ref](signature) declares the native reference element emitted for a labelled highlight.

 Signature

typst code
// Create a highlight reference element
codly.highlight-ref(
  body,
  block: label,
  line: int,
  by: "line" | "item",
  item: content | none = none,
  separator: auto | str | content = auto,
  numbering: auto | function | none = auto
)

// Set default fields for matching highlight references
codly.highlight-ref-set_(..args)

// Install a replacement callback or content for matching highlight references
codly.highlight-ref-show_(it, ..args)


 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content \| none | Required, positional | Reference body supplied by Typst. |
| block | label | Required, named | Label of the containing code block. |
| line | int | Required, named | Displayed line number containing the highlight. |
| item | content \| none | none | Highlight tag used when by is "item". |
| by | "line" \| "item" | Required, named | Whether to show the line number or highlight tag. |
| separator | auto \| str \| content \| none | auto | Text between the block reference and this reference; auto uses [codly.ref](ref.md) settings. |
| numbering | auto \| function \| none | auto | Formatter for line references; auto uses [codly.ref](ref.md) settings. |

 Behavior

Typst emits this element when a native reference targets a label on a highlight. It retains the reference to the containing figure or code block, so native figure numbering and links work. With by: "line", the formatter receives the displayed line number. With by: "item", the tag is shown and item must be present. A none formatter suppresses the numeric part of line references; item references still show their tag. The default separator and formatter come from [codly.ref](ref.md).

[codly.highlight-ref-set_(..args)](signature) sets fields for matching references. [codly.highlight-ref-show_(it, ..args)](signature) installs a replacement callback or content for the matching element; a callback receives the reference element. These wrappers follow the same scoped show-rule model as other Codly elements.

 Example

typ preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.highlight-ref-set_(numbering: numbering.with("H1"))

The marked line is @marked.

figure(caption: [A labelled highlight])[
  codly.new(
    
    answer = 42
    ,
    highlights: ((line: 1, start: 0, end: 6, label:  ),),
  )
]

title: annotation-ref
text:
codly.annotation-ref

> [!WARNING] References need a labelled figure.
> To use references to annotations, you must ensure that the Codly code block is contained within a labelled figure. 

A native reference element created for a labelled annotation in a code block inside a figure.

 Signature

typst code
// Create a new annotation reference.
codly.annotation-ref(body, block: label, line: int, item: content, by: "line" | "item", suffix: none, separator: auto, numbering: auto)

// Equivalent set-rule for an annotation reference.
codly.annotation-ref-set_(..args)

// Override the show-rule for an annotation reference.
codly.annotation-ref-show_(it, ..args)


Codly creates this element when Typst resolves a native reference such as @note. Use annotation-ref-set_(...) to set fields in scope, or annotation-ref-show_(callback) to replace or transform its display. The show wrapper accepts a callback or content, as supported by the element show-rule API.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content or none | required | Internal body of the native reference. |
| block | label | required | Label of the containing code block. |
| line | int | required | Displayed source line associated with the annotation. |
| item | content | required | Annotation content used for item references. |
| suffix | content or none | none | Optional suffix after the formatted line number. |
| by | "line" \| "item" | required | Whether the suffix shows a formatted line number or the annotation item. |
| separator | auto \| str \| content \| none | auto | Content between the native block reference and its suffix; auto uses [codly.ref](ref.md) settings. |
| numbering | auto \| function \| none | auto | Line-number formatter; auto uses [codly.ref](ref.md) settings and none omits the suffix in line mode. |

by, separator, and numbering can also be set for all generated references with [codly.ref](ref.md). Explicit fields on this element take precedence. In item mode, the annotation's content is used; numbering and suffix apply only to line mode. With line mode and numbering: none, the rendered reference contains just the native reference to the code block.

annotation-ref-show_ receives the generated reference element, so a callback can inspect or wrap it. For example, show: codly.annotation-ref-show_(it => [Note: it]) prefixes each displayed annotation reference while keeping its existing rendering.

 Example: Basic usage

The item-mode reference uses the annotation content after the code figure reference:

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

figure(caption: [A code example])[
  codly.new(
    
    first line
    second line
    ,
    annotations: ((start: 2, label:  , content: [the note]),),
  )
] 

The annotation reference is @note.



 Example: Item-based reference

The item-mode reference uses the annotation content after the code figure reference:

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.ref-set_(by: "item", sep: " — ")
show: codly.annotation-ref-show_(it => [Note: it])

figure(caption: [A code example])[
  codly.new(
    
    first line
    second line
    ,
    annotations: ((start: 2, label:  , content: [the note]),),
  )
] 

The annotation reference is @note.

title: sublang-block
text:
codly.sublang-block

> [!WARNING] Sublang blocks performance may be impacted.
> Sublang blocks may degrade performance, due to the requirement of re-parsing and leveraging introspection for each sublang block.

The generated element that holds one syntax-highlighted language range inside a Codly code block.

 Signature

typst code
codly.sublang-block(body, idx)


Codly creates this element while rendering [codly.new](new.md). In normal use, configure language ranges with the block's sublangs field and [codly.sublang](../types/sublang.md), rather than constructing this element directly. Both required fields are positional in the generated element constructor.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content | Required, positional | Raw block content highlighted with the range's language. |
| idx | int | Required, positional | Zero-based index of this range in the block's sublangs array. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Range indexes follow declaration order.
> idx is zero-based within one code block's sublangs array; it does not
> identify a source line or language key.

For each configured sublanguage range, Codly creates a raw block using that range's language and stores it in body. Its display preserves the raw block's syntax highlighting while attaching metadata to each source line so the block renderer can apply the corresponding highlighted line content. idx distinguishes ranges in the same code block; it is assigned from their order in sublangs.

 Example

The shell lines use the outer language, while the Rust lines use the language selected for source lines 2–4.

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  sh
  > cat test.rs
  fn main() {
      println!("hello");
  }
  > exit

  ,
  sublangs: ((start: 2, end: 4, lang: "rs"),),
)
