title: language
text:
codly.language

Defines the displayed name, color, and optional icon for a language badge in a code block.

 Signature

typst code
codly.language(
  name: str | content,
  color: paint | none = none,
  icon: str | content | none = none,
)


name is required and named. Fields expecting this type also accept a string as shorthand for name, or a dictionary. Unknown fields are retained.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name | str \| content | Required | Displayed language name. |
| color | paint \| none | none | Language color; none uses the badge's default color. |
| icon | str \| content \| none | none | Optional icon shown beside the name. |

The declaration preserves additional, unknown fields. They can provide language-specific overrides to [codly.lang](../components/lang.md) fields, such as radius or fill.

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Keep badge styling with each language.
> Additional fields are preserved, so a language entry can set badge fields
> such as radius or fill just for that language.

Use language definitions as values in the languages dictionary passed to [codly.lang-set_](../components/lang.mdsignature). The dictionary key must match the raw block's language tag. The settings apply within the show rule's scope. A definition's name, icon, and color customize the badge; an omitted definition falls back to the raw language tag. A definition's matching [codly.lang](../components/lang.md) style fields override the corresponding settings supplied to [codly.lang-set_](../components/lang.mdsignature).

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.lang-set_(languages: (
  rs: (name: [Rust], color: rgb("b7502a"), icon: "R"),
))
show raw.where(block: true): codly.new

rs
fn main() {
    println!("Hello, Rust!");
}

title: range
text:
codly.range

Selects an inclusive range of one-indexed source lines for a code block.

 Signature

typst code
codly.range(start, end: none)


start is positional and required. end is optional and may be passed positionally or by name.

 Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| start | int | Required | First source line to display, counting from 1. |
| end | int \| none | none | Last source line to display, inclusive. none selects through the end of the block. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> Range endpoints count source lines from one and include both start and
> end; displayed numbering offsets do not change them.

> [!TIP] Adjacent ranges merge.
> When several ranges are selected, Codly sorts them and merges overlapping
> or directly adjacent ranges before rendering.

Pass a range to [codly.new](../components/new.md)'s range field, or pass several ranges to its ranges field. These coordinates refer to source lines, independently of displayed line-number offsets. The range is inclusive at both ends; an open range such as [codly.range(3)](signature) continues through the final source line.

The constructor accepts positional arguments ([codly.range(2, 4)](signature)) or named arguments ([codly.range(start: 2, end: 4)](signature)). Its implicit casts accept a one- or two-element array, or a dictionary with start and optional end keys. For example, (2, 4) and (start: 2, end: 4) cast to the same value as the constructor. Unknown dictionary keys are rejected. Inputs are type-checked as integers (or none for end); the range type does not impose a positivity or ordering constraint.

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  
  prepare()
  validate()
  transform()
  save()
  ,
  range: codly.range(2, 3),
)

title: skip
text:
codly.skip

Describes an explicit collapsed gap in a code block; pass it in [codly.new](../components/new.md)'s skips field.

 Signature

typst code
codly.skip(position, length: 1)


position is the required positional argument; length is optional and can be supplied positionally or by name.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| position | int | Required | Zero-indexed source position where the skip row is inserted. |
| length | int | 1 | Number of omitted lines represented by the skip; added to subsequent displayed line numbers. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> position is a zero-indexed source position, even when ranges or offsets
> change which lines appear.

> [!TIP] Duplicate positions make one skip row.
> If multiple skips have the same position, Codly uses the first entry's
> length to adjust subsequent displayed line numbers.

The constructor accepts [codly.skip(position, length)](signature) or named fields. A dictionary casts using position and optional length; an array of one or two values casts positionally. Other array lengths and unrelated values fail to cast. The skips field sorts entries by position; duplicate records at one position produce one skip row, and only the first record's length affects the numbering offset. Positions refer to source lines even when ranges or offsets affect what is displayed.

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  text
  first
  second
  third
  fourth
  ,
  skips: (codly.skip(2, 4),),
)

title: highlighted-line
text:
codly.highlighted-line

Describes one whole line to highlight in [codly.new](../components/new.md).

 Signature

typst code
codly.highlighted-line(line, color: none)


line is required and positional; color is optional and positional or named.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| line | int | Required | One-indexed displayed line number to highlight. |
| color | none \| paint | none | Optional paint for this line; none uses the next color from [codly.highlight](../components/highlight.md). |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Uses displayed line numbers
> line refers to the number shown in the document, including offsets and numbering changes from skips. A source line with no displayed number cannot be selected this way.

> [!TIP] Explicit colors leave the palette cycle untouched
> A supplied color is used directly. Entries with color: none take and advance the next [codly.highlight](../components/highlight.md) palette color.

The constructor also accepts named fields. The value casts from an integer, a dictionary with line and optional color, or an array of one or two values in field order. Other values and arrays of other lengths fail to cast. The line number refers to the displayed numbering, including offsets and numbering changes caused by skips; a line with no displayed number cannot be highlighted this way. An explicit color is used directly and does not advance the [codly.highlight](../components/highlight.md) palette; entries with color: none use and advance that palette in declaration order.

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  text
  prepare()
  run()
  cleanup()
  ,
  highlighted: (codly.highlighted-line(2, yellow.lighten(75%)),),
)

title: unnumbered-line
text:
codly.unnumbered-line

Selects a source line to show without its line number, optionally putting content in the number cell.

 Signature

typst code
codly.unnumbered-line(line, fill: [])


Both arguments are positional: line is required and fill is optional.

 Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| line | int | Required | One-indexed source line to display without a line number. |
| fill | content | [] | Content to display in the number cell instead. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> line is a one-indexed source line, even when a range or offset changes its
> displayed position or number.

> [!TIP] Later line numbers stay contiguous.
> An unnumbered line does not advance the displayed sequence. You can refer to
> consecutive unnumbered lines with @block:l2p1, @block:l2p2, and so on.

Pass entries to [codly.new](../components/new.md)'s unnumbered field. The constructor takes positional arguments; implicit casts accept an integer, a one- or two-element array, or a dictionary with line and optional fill fields. Array values are positional, and other array lengths do not cast. The coordinates always refer to source lines, even when ranges or offsets change which lines appear or their displayed numbers.

An unnumbered line does not advance the displayed number sequence, so later numbered lines remain contiguous. Consecutive unnumbered lines can be referenced with labels such as @block:l2p1 and @block:l2p2, where the l number is the preceding displayed number and p counts the unnumbered lines after it.

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

figure(caption: [Unnumbered source lines])[
  codly.new(
    
    first
    label:
    second
    end
    last
    ,
    unnumbered: (
      codly.unnumbered-line(2, [↳]),
      codly.unnumbered-line(4),
    ),
  )
] 

The unnumbered lines are @block:l1p1 and @block:l2p1.

title: smart-skip
text:
codly.smart-skip

Configures which omitted source-line gaps appear as collapsed skip rows when a code block displays selected ranges.

 Signature

typst code
codly.smart-skip(
  first: bool | none = none,
  last: bool | none = none,
  rest: bool | none = none,
)


All fields are named and optional.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| first | bool \| none | none | Include a skip when source lines before the first selected range are omitted. |
| last | bool \| none | none | Include a skip when source lines after the last selected range are omitted. |
| rest | bool \| none | none | Include skips for omitted lines between selected ranges or otherwise in the middle of the block. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> Automatic skips mark gaps between displayed source ranges; they do not
> change the source-line coordinates used by those ranges.

> [!TIP] Configure the three gap locations independently.
> first controls omitted lines before the first range, rest controls gaps
> between ranges, and last controls omitted lines after the last range.

Pass this value to [codly.new](../components/new.md)'s smart-skip field. A boolean casts to the same value for all three fields. A dictionary casts to this type: omitted rest defaults to false, and omitted first or last inherits rest. Thus (rest: true, first: false) enables middle skips and trailing skips, while suppressing a leading skip. With all three fields false, no automatic skips are inserted. A skip row is inserted only for a discontinuity in the displayed source lines; its represented length is the number of omitted lines.

 Example: Basic Usage

yaml widgets
- type: switch
  name: show-middle-gap
  label: Show the omitted middle lines
  default: true


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  python
  def prepare():
      load_data()
      validate()
      transform()
      save()
      report()
      cleanup()
  ,
  ranges: ((2, 3), (6, 7)),
  smart-skip: codly.smart-skip(first: false, last: false, rest: show-middle-gap),
)

title: highlight-config
text:
codly.highlight-config

Describes one character-level highlight on a source line in a Codly code block. See [codly.new](../components/new.md) for the block's highlights field.

 Signature

typst code
codly.highlight-config(line, start: none, end: none, fill: none, tag: none, inset: none, baseline: none, clip: none, outset: none, radius: none, label: none, stroke: none, depth: none)


line is the required positional field; every other field is named. A dictionary with a line key can also be cast to this type.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| line | int | Required | One-indexed displayed line number to highlight; must be greater than zero. |
| start | none \| int | none | Zero-indexed character position where the highlight starts; none becomes 0. |
| end | none \| int | none | Exclusive zero-indexed end bound; none extends to the end of the line. |
| fill | none \| paint \| function | none | Explicit paint, or a callback receiving the next palette paint; none uses the configured palette. |
| tag | none \| str \| content | none | Optional tag displayed with the highlight. |
| inset | none \| length \| dictionary | none | Overrides [codly.highlight](../components/highlight.md)'s inset. |
| baseline | none \| length \| auto | none | Overrides the highlight box baseline; auto preserves the content baseline. |
| clip | none \| bool | none | Overrides [codly.highlight](../components/highlight.md)'s clip. |
| outset | none \| length \| dictionary | none | Overrides [codly.highlight](../components/highlight.md)'s outset. |
| radius | none \| length | none | Overrides [codly.highlight](../components/highlight.md)'s radius. |
| label | none \| label | none | Label for referencing this highlight; labels apply only when the code block is inside a figure. |
| stroke | none \| stroke \| function | none | Overrides [codly.highlight](../components/highlight.md)'s stroke. |
| depth | none \| int | none | Controls stacking when highlights overlap; larger values appear on top. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> line is a one-indexed displayed line number, including any offset.
> start and end are zero-indexed character positions, and end is exclusive.

> [!WARNING] References need a labelled figure
> To reference a highlight, give it a label and place its code block inside a labelled figure.

The constructor and dictionary cast normalize omitted or none bounds to start: 0 and an end bound covering the rest of the line. Explicit bounds must be nonnegative; line must be positive. Character positions are zero-indexed and the end is exclusive, unlike the inclusive, one-indexed source-line ranges. A fill paint is used directly and does not consume a palette entry; a callback receives the next palette paint. Highlights using none also consume the next palette entry. An empty configured palette is invalid. Local style fields override the corresponding [codly.highlight](../components/highlight.md) settings when provided.

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  py
  let answer = 42
  ,
  highlights: (codly.highlight-config(1, start: 4, end: 10, fill: yellow.lighten(65%), tag: "value"),),
)

title: annotation-config
text:
codly.annotation-config

Describes an annotation attached to one or more one-indexed source lines in a code block.

 Signature

typst code
codly.annotation-config(start, end: none, content: none, label: none, numbering: n => [n])


 Parameters

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| start | int | required | First source line covered by the annotation; must be greater than zero. |
| end | int \| none | none | Last covered line. none is normalized to start; otherwise it must be positive and at least start. |
| content | content \| none | none | Showable content displayed beside the annotation; none leaves only its number. |
| label | label \| none | none | Label for referencing this annotation when its code block is inside a figure. |
| numbering | function \| none | n => [n] | Function formatting the annotation number. Set to none to hide the number. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> start and end are one-indexed source lines, and end is inclusive. Displayed line-number offsets do not change the covered source lines.

> [!WARNING] References need a labelled figure
> To reference an annotation, give it a label and place its code block inside a labelled figure. Codly discovers the figure label automatically.

> [!WARNING] Annotation ranges cannot overlap.
> Two annotations cannot cover the same source line. Because end is
> inclusive, the next annotation must start after the previous one's end.

The positional start argument is required. The constructor also accepts a dictionary with a start key. Dictionary and constructor inputs are type-checked, then normalized: a missing or none end becomes start, and missing content becomes none. start and a supplied end must be positive, and end must not precede start.

Annotations are passed in the code block's annotations array. Their source-line ranges must not overlap. An annotation range is expressed in source-line coordinates, independent of any displayed line-number offset.

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  py
  prepare()
  result = compute()
  print(result)
  cleanup()
  ,
  annotations: (
    codly.annotation-config(
      2,
      end: 3,
      content: [These lines compute and display the result.],
    ),
  ),
)

title: callout-config
text:
codly.callout-config

Describes a content row attached to a source line in a code block. Use it in the callouts field of [codly.new](../components/new.md).

 Signature

typst code
codly.callout-config(line: int, body: content, align: auto, breakable: auto, inset: auto, fill: auto, stroke: auto, source-indent: auto, placement: auto, bubble-gap: auto, pointer: auto, pointer-align: auto, pointer-size: auto, pointer-height: auto, pointer-width: auto, pointer-offset: auto, bubble-align: auto, bubble-fill: auto, bubble-stroke: auto, bubble-inset: auto, bubble-outset: auto, bubble-radius: auto, bubble-width: auto)


All fields are named. A dictionary with line and body keys can also be used as a callout entry.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| line | int | Required | One-indexed source line to attach the callout to; must be greater than zero. |
| body | content | Required | Content displayed in the callout row. |
| align | alignment \| auto \| none | auto | Alignment of the callout cell; auto inherits the element setting. |
| breakable | bool \| auto \| none | auto | Whether the cell may break across pages; auto inherits the element setting. |
| inset | length \| dictionary \| auto \| none | auto | Callout cell inset; auto inherits the element setting. |
| fill | paint \| auto \| none | auto | Callout cell fill; auto inherits the element setting. |
| stroke | stroke \| auto \| none | auto | Callout cell stroke; auto inherits the element setting. |
| source-indent | bool \| auto | auto | Aligns a plain callout with its source indentation while reserving gutter columns. Pointed bubbles remain anchored to their character. |
| placement | "above" \| "below" \| auto | auto | Side of the source line for the row or bubble. |
| bubble-gap | length \| dictionary \| auto | auto | Minimum distance between neighboring bubbles; use a length for both axes or (x: length, y: length). |
| pointer | int \| none \| auto | auto | Character anchor in the source line: one-indexed, with 0 at line start. none disables the bubble. |
| pointer-align | "start" \| "center" \| "end" \| auto | auto | Preferred bubble alignment around its source character; placement clamps it to the row. |
| pointer-size | length \| auto | auto | Arrow height and half of its base width. |
| pointer-height | length \| auto | auto | Arrow height; auto uses pointer-size. |
| pointer-width | length \| auto | auto | Full arrow base width; auto uses twice pointer-size. |
| pointer-offset | length \| auto | auto | Horizontal shift of the arrow tip from the character anchor; positive is right, negative is left, and the tip is clamped to the bubble. |
| bubble-align | alignment \| auto | auto | Alignment of bubble content, independent of callout cell alignment. |
| bubble-fill | paint \| none \| auto | auto | Fill shared by the bubble and arrow. |
| bubble-stroke | stroke \| none \| auto | auto | The bubble's single outline. |
| bubble-inset | length \| dictionary \| auto | auto | Padding inside the bubble. |
| bubble-outset | length \| dictionary \| auto | auto | Extra paint extent around the padded body, reserved in the row. |
| bubble-radius | length \| auto | auto | Bubble corner radius. |
| bubble-width | length \| ratio \| auto | auto | Preferred padded body width; auto fits content, bounded by the available row. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> line is a one-indexed source line. pointer is a one-indexed character position after any diff marker is removed; 0 points to the start of the line.

> [!WARNING] Pointed bubble groups stay together
> Bubbles attached to a source line stay together on one page, so a group may move as a unit at a page break.

An entry's auto style values inherit from [codly.callout](../components/callout.md); bubble styles can then inherit from [codly.bubble](../components/bubble.md). Explicit entry values take precedence. Cell fill and stroke accept none to disable painting. A pointed bubble uses one shared outline and paint for its body and arrow, and wraps its content at the available width.

The callout attaches using source-line coordinates, unaffected by displayed line-number offsets or diff markers. Pointer positions count characters in the source line after a diff marker is removed; unlike highlight bounds, they are one-indexed, except that zero denotes the start. The pointer follows the rendered character when source text wraps. Bubble groups stay together on a page. Consecutive bubbles on the same side with matching cell styles share a row when their outlines fit; overlaps use another lane in declaration order.

Negative pointer positions, dimensions, insets, outsets, and gaps are invalid. bubble-gap dictionaries accept only x and y, whose omitted values default to 0.5em.

 Example: Basic Usage

yaml widgets
- type: slider
  name: bubble-width
  label: Bubble width
  default: 120pt
  unit: pt
  min: 80
  max: 180
  step: 10


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  py
  if ready:
    start()
  ,
  callouts: (
    codly.callout-config(
      line: 2,
      pointer: 5,
      body: [This call runs when the input is ready.],
      bubble-width: bubble-width,
      bubble-fill: aqua.lighten(80%),
    ),
  ),
)

title: gutter-column
text:
codly.gutter-column

Defines one independently styled column beside a code block. Use it in gutters to show source-line labels, markers, or other row-specific content.

 Signature

typst code
codly.gutter-column(
  values: array  | function,
  width: auto | length | ratio | fraction = auto,
  align: auto | alignment = auto,
  inset: auto | length | dictionary = auto,
  stroke: auto | stroke | dictionary | none = auto,
  fill: auto | paint | array  | function | none = auto,
  text: dictionary = (:),
)


values is required and named. Arrays and functions can also be passed directly as gutter column specifications; dictionaries are cast to this type.

 Parameters

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| values | array  or function | Required | Values to display, or a callback that returns a value for a rendered row. |
| width | auto, length, ratio, or fraction | auto | Column width. |
| align | auto or alignment | auto | Cell alignment. |
| inset | auto, length, or dictionary | auto | Cell inset. |
| stroke | auto, stroke, dictionary, or none | auto | Cell stroke. |
| fill | auto, paint, array , function, or none | auto | Cell fill, a row-indexed fill palette, or a row callback. |
| text | dictionary | (:) | Arguments passed to text when displaying a value. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Array values follow source lines
> An array entry at index 0 supplies source line 1, even with ranges or
> offsets. Missing entries and none leave the gutter cell empty.

> [!TIP] Use a callback for rendered-row logic
> Only code and skip rows have gutter cells. A callback receives both
> source-line and kind, so it can handle skip rows separately from code.

Array values are indexed by one-based source line, even when a code block uses ranges, offsets, or generated skip rows. Missing entries and none leave a cell empty. A callback receives the rendered row dictionary with index, kind, source-line, number, and text. index counts displayed rows, including headers and callouts; source-line is one-based for source rows and none for generated rows. Callbacks may return content, strings, numbers, or none.

Only code and skip rows have gutter cells. Values are validated when resolved, and width must be non-negative. auto alignment and insets inherit the number column's settings; fill: auto follows the body row. A fill callback also receives the row dictionary, with text populated from the source line where available.

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  
  let answer = 42
  print(answer)
  ,
  gutters: (
    codly.gutter-column(
      values: row => if row.kind == "code" {
        str(row.source-line) + ". " + row.text
      } else { none },
      align: right,
      inset: (left: 4pt, right: 8pt),
      fill: gray.lighten(90%),
    ),
  ),
)

title: diff
text:
codly.diff

Configures automatic parsing, syntax highlighting, gutters, and row fills for raw blocks whose language is diff, .

 Signature

typst code
codly.diff(
  enabled: bool = true,
  added-fill: auto | paint | function = rgb("dafbe1"),
  removed-fill: auto | paint | function = rgb("ffebe9"),
  meta-fill: auto | paint | function = rgb("ddf4ff"),
  context-fill: auto | paint | function = auto,
  numbers: bool = true,
  markers: bool = true,
  added-marker: str | content = "+",
  removed-marker: str | content = "−",
  old-offset: int = 0,
  new-offset: int = 0,
)


The fields can also be supplied as a dictionary. A boolean casts to enabled.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enabled | bool | true | Enables diff processing. |
| added-fill | auto \| paint \| function \| none | rgb("dafbe1") | Fill for added rows. |
| removed-fill | auto \| paint \| function \| none | rgb("ffebe9") | Fill for removed rows. |
| meta-fill | auto \| paint \| function \| none | rgb("ddf4ff") | Fill for patch metadata rows. |
| context-fill | auto \| paint \| function \| none | auto | Fill for unchanged rows; auto follows the ordinary row fill. |
| numbers | bool | true | Shows automatic old-side and new-side line-number gutters. |
| markers | bool | true | Shows the automatic added/removed marker gutter. |
| added-marker | str \| content | "+" | Marker shown for added rows. |
| removed-marker | str \| content | "−" | Marker shown for removed rows. |
| old-offset | int | 0 | Added to old-side source line numbers. |
| new-offset | int | 0 | Added to new-side source line numbers. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Use the patch language prefix
> Set the raw block language to diff, , such as diff,py, to enable patch parsing and highlight the changed code as Python.

> [!NOTE] Patch line coordinates
> References and line-based settings use displayed patch-row numbers. Highlight and callout character positions count code after the diff marker is removed.

> [!WARNING] Combined merge diffs are unsupported
> Codly parses unified patches, including multiple files and hunks, but not combined merge diff format.

Codly detects diff,  when the block-level diff setting is auto (the default). It removes the diff, prefix for syntax highlighting and renders old and new source views separately, so removed code does not affect new-side syntax state. Unified patches may contain multiple files and hunks; each is highlighted independently. Combined merge diffs are unsupported. A non-patch snippet may use  , +, and - prefixes for context, added, and removed rows.

Each fill accepts a paint, none, or auto; auto uses the ordinary row fill. A callback receives the row with a diff record containing kind, old, and new line coordinates, as well as the row's usual fields. Explicit highlights take precedence over diff fills. Setting diff: false or diff: none disables processing; setting it to true enables the default configuration. Custom gutters replace the automatic old/new/marker columns.

References and line-based settings use displayed patch-row numbers. Character positions for highlights and callouts refer to code after its diff marker is removed.

 Example: Basic Usage

yaml widgets
- type: switch
  name: diff-enabled
  label: Process the diff
  default: true


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  diff,py
   shared
  -old = 1
  +new = 2
   tail
  ,
  diff: if diff-enabled { auto } else { false },
)

title: sublang
text:
codly.sublang

Assigns a syntax-highlighting language to an inclusive range of source lines in a code block.

 Signature

typst code
codly.sublang(
  start: int,
  end: int,
  lang: str,
)


All fields are required and named. The value can also be supplied as a dictionary.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| start | int | Required | First source line in the range, counting from 1. |
| end | int | Required | Last source line in the range, inclusive. |
| lang | str | Required | Syntax-highlighting language key used for these lines. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> Sublanguage ranges count one-indexed source lines and include both
> endpoints, independent of displayed line-number offsets.

> [!TIP] Highlighting preserves the original lines.
> Codly applies each range's syntax language to its source lines while keeping
> their text and positions in the outer code block.

Pass one or more [codly.sublang](signature) values in the sublangs argument to [codly.new](../components/new.md). start must be greater than zero, and end must be at least start; invalid ranges raise an error. Each range is counted from the first line of the raw block, independently of line-number offsets. Lines in the range are highlighted with the selected language's syntax while retaining their original source text and line positions. Lines outside the ranges keep the raw block's language. Ranges may be supplied as dictionaries with the same three fields.

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  sh
  echo before
  fn answer() {
      42
  }
  echo after

  ,
  sublangs: (
    (start: 2, end: 4, lang: "rs"),
  ),
)

title: rainbow
text:
codly.rainbow

Configures syntax-aware coloring for matching code delimiters by nesting depth.

 Signature

typst code
codly.rainbow(
  enabled: bool = true,
  palette: array  = (...),
  pairs: array  = ("()", "[]", "{}"),
  depth-offset: int = 0,
  unmatched: color | none = none,
  code-scopes: str = ...,
  ignore-scopes: str = ...,
)


The value can also be a dictionary with these fields, or a boolean that sets enabled.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enabled | bool | true | Enables delimiter coloring. |
| palette | array  | Built-in palette | Colors cycled by nesting depth; must not be empty. |
| pairs | array of "()" \| "[]" \| "{}" | ("()", "[]", "{}") | Delimiter pairs recognized for nesting. |
| depth-offset | int | 0 | Adds an offset to the nesting depth before choosing a palette color; must be nonnegative. |
| unmatched | color \| none | none | Color for unmatched delimiters; none leaves their syntax color unchanged. |
| code-scopes | str | Built-in selectors | Syntax scope selectors classified as code by the rainbow pass. |
| ignore-scopes | str | Built-in selectors | Syntax scope selectors excluded from delimiter coloring, such as strings and comments. |

 Behavior

> [!WARNING] The palette must be nonempty.
> An empty palette or a negative depth-offset causes a compilation error.

> [!TIP] Adjust scopes for unusual grammars.
> code-scopes and ignore-scopes replace the built-in selectors. Customize
> them when a language classifies delimiters differently from the defaults.

Set rainbow on [codly.new](../components/new.md) or in [codly.set_](../components/new.mdbehavior) to configure blocks in that scope. true enables the defaults and false disables the pass. Delimiters are colored according to nesting depth, cycling through palette; depth-offset shifts the starting color. Only pairs listed in pairs contribute to nesting. Unclosed openers and unmatched closers use unmatched when it is a color; otherwise they retain their syntax highlighting.

The pass uses syntax scopes to find code and ignore literals and comments. code-scopes and ignore-scopes replace the built-in selector strings, so customize them when a language's grammar classifies delimiters differently. Sublanguage regions are processed with their own nesting stack.

 Example: Basic Usage

yaml widgets
- type: switch
  name: rainbow-enabled
  label: Color delimiters
  default: true
- type: select
  name: rainbow-pairs
  label: Delimiter pairs
  default: '("()", "[]", "{}")'
  options:
    - label: All pairs
      value: '("()", "[]", "{}")'
    - label: Braces only
      value: '("{}",)'


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  rs
  fn main() {
      let items = [1, 2, 3];
      println!("{}", items[0]);
  }
  ,
  rainbow: if rainbow-enabled {
    (palette: (rgb("d73a49"), rgb("005cc5"), rgb("22863a")), pairs: rainbow-pairs)
  } else {
    false
  },
)

title: indent-guides
text:
codly.indent-guides

Configures optional vertical guides at complete indentation levels in a code block.

 Signature

typst code
codly.indent-guides(
  enabled: bool = true,
  width: auto | int = auto,
  blank-lines: bool = true,
  rainbow: auto | bool = auto,
  palette: auto | array  = auto,
  depth-offset: auto | int = auto,
  color: color = luma(70%),
  thickness: length = 0.5pt,
  x-offset: length = 0pt,
)


The fields can also be supplied as a dictionary. A boolean casts to enabled.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enabled | bool | true | Draws indentation guides when enabled. |
| width | auto \| int | auto | Spaces per indentation level. auto votes on observed indentation changes. |
| blank-lines | bool | true | Continues shared guide levels across interior blank lines. |
| rainbow | auto \| bool | auto | Colors guides by level; auto follows whether delimiter rainbow coloring is enabled. |
| palette | auto \| array  | auto | Nonempty colors for rainbow guides; auto shares the delimiter palette. |
| depth-offset | auto \| int | auto | Nonnegative palette offset; auto shares the delimiter offset. |
| color | color | luma(70%) | Guide color when rainbow coloring is disabled. |
| thickness | length | 0.5pt | Positive stroke thickness. |
| x-offset | length | 0pt | Horizontal guide shift; positive moves right and negative moves left. Supports em lengths. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Check the inferred indentation step
> width: auto chooses the most frequently observed change in leading spaces; ties favor the smaller step, and no observed step falls back to four spaces. Set width explicitly when the source uses a known indentation size.

> [!NOTE] Only complete levels get guides
> A guide is drawn for each complete width-sized level. Indentation that does not reach the next complete level has no guide.

Set the block-level indent-guides field to true to use defaults, to false to disable inherited guides for one block, or to a configuration to customize them. width: auto infers the step from observed changes in leading spaces; an explicit width sets spaces per level. A level is drawn only for complete indentation steps. Interior blank lines continue only the levels shared by the surrounding nonblank lines when blank-lines is true; leading and trailing blank lines have no inferred guides.

With rainbow: auto, guides use delimiter rainbow colors when delimiter rainbow is enabled. Explicit rainbow: true enables palette coloring; false uses color. An explicit palette or depth offset overrides values inherited from delimiter rainbow settings. The palette must not be empty, width must be positive or auto, depth offset must be nonnegative or auto, and thickness must be positive. Invalid field types are rejected by the declared types.

Guides follow source indentation and extend across wrapped visual rows when smart indentation is enabled. x-offset shifts all guides horizontally without changing source columns.

 Example: Basic Usage

yaml widgets
- type: switch
  name: guides-enabled
  label: Show indentation guides
  default: true
- type: select
  name: guide-width
  label: Spaces per level
  default: '4'
  options:
    - label: Two spaces
      value: '2'
    - label: Four spaces
      value: '4'
    - label: Eight spaces
      value: '8'


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  text
  root
      child
          leaf
      sibling
  root
  ,
  indent-guides: if guides-enabled { (width: guide-width) } else { false },
)

title: Themes and helpers
text:
Themes and helpers

Use themes to apply consistent component styles and info to inspect a labelled block in context.

> [!TIP] Apply themes in scope.
> Use show: codly.theme(...) before the code blocks you want to style.
> Put the rule inside a content block to limit it to that part of the document.

- [codly.theme](theme.md)
- [codly.themes](themes.md)
- [codly.define-theme](define-theme.md)
- [codly.info](info.md)

title: theme
text:
codly.theme

Returns scoped set and show rules that apply a built-in or custom theme to Codly elements.

 Signature

typst code
codly.theme(..options)


 Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| preset (positional) | str or dictionary | "thesis" | Built-in theme name or a theme dictionary. At most one positional value is accepted. |
| Named options | See [codly.define-theme](define-theme.md) | None | Shared tokens and element dictionaries forwarded to [codly.define-theme](define-theme.md). |

The built-in presets are "thesis", "dark", "clean", "github-light", "solarized-light", and "one-light". The "thesis" preset follows Codly's ordinary visual defaults. See [codly.themes](themes.md) for the preset dictionaries and [codly.define-theme](define-theme.md) for supported shared tokens, element dictionaries, and merge behavior.

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Theme only Codly content.
> The theme's typography and syntax colors apply inside Codly blocks; ordinary raw text outside them keeps its own styling.

Use the returned function as a show rule, commonly show: codly.theme("dark"). It applies scoped set rules to Codly's block, line, number, language, file, header, footer, highlight, callout, bubble, and annotation elements, along with their typography and syntax colors.

Named options are passed to [codly.define-theme](define-theme.md), which validates names and values and combines them with the selected preset. Explicit element fields and later local set rules keep their normal precedence.

 Example: Basic Usage

Choose a preset to preview it on a code block:

yaml widgets
- type: select
  name: theme-preset
  label: Theme
  default: '"github-light"'
  options:
    - label: Thesis
      value: '"thesis"'
    - label: Dark
      value: '"dark"'
    - label: Clean
      value: '"clean"'
    - label: GitHub Light
      value: '"github-light"'
    - label: Solarized Light
      value: '"solarized-light"'
    - label: One Light
      value: '"one-light"'


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.theme(theme-preset)
codly.new(
  py
  def double(value):
      return value  2
  ,
  header: [example.py],
)

title: themes
text:
codly.themes

The built-in theme dictionaries, keyed by preset name; use [codly.theme](theme.md) to render one or [codly.define-theme](define-theme.md) to derive a reusable configuration.

 Signature

typst code
codly.themes: dictionary


Its six keys are thesis, dark, clean, github-light, solarized-light, and one-light. Each value is a theme dictionary. thesis is Codly's default appearance.

| Preset | Appearance |
| --- | --- |
| thesis | Codly's ordinary defaults, with language-colored badges and a light header. |
| dark | Dark editor palette with light text and syntax colors. |
| clean | Unboxed code with muted text and unpainted language badges. |
| github-light | GitHub light editor palette. |
| solarized-light | Solarized light editor palette. |
| one-light | One Light editor palette. |

 Theme dictionary keys

The theme loader accepts these shared token keys and element-section keys. Unknown top-level keys are rejected.

| Kind | Keys | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shared token | foreground, muted, fill, accent, stroke, radius, inset | Main text, subdued text, code-line fill, accent color, outline, corner radius, and inner spacing. |
| Shared token | header-fill, footer-fill, bubble-fill | Fills for headers, footers, and callout bubbles. |
| Shared token | syntax, highlight-fill, highlight-colors, language-colors | Raw-code syntax theme, highlight fill, highlight color or palette, and whether language badges use their language colors. |
| Element section | block, line, number, lang, file, header, footer, highlight, callout, bubble, annotation | A dictionary of settings for that Codly element. Fields within a section follow that element's settings; its text field accepts native Typst text settings. |

The public theme dictionary can be inspected or selected by key. For the exact merge behavior and validation when creating a custom dictionary, see [codly.define-theme](define-theme.md).

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Derive a custom preset.
> Pass a value such as codly.themes.dark as base to [codly.define-theme](define-theme.md) to start a custom theme from that preset.

The preset entries are complete theme dictionaries; looking up a preset does not apply it to the document by itself.

 Example: Basic Usage

This renders one code block for each built-in preset so their appearances can be compared side by side.

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

let source = py
def double(value):
    return value  2

grid(
  columns: (1fr, 1fr),
  gutter: 6pt,
  ..codly.themes.keys().map(name => {
    show: codly.theme(name)
    codly.new(source, header: [name])
  }),
)

title: define-theme
text:
codly.define-theme

Build a reusable theme dictionary by inheriting a built-in preset or another theme, then applying named token and element-setting overrides.

 Signature

typst code
codly.define-theme(base: "thesis", ..overrides)


base is named and defaults to "thesis"; overrides are named arguments. Positional arguments are not accepted.

 Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base | str or dictionary | "thesis" | A preset name or an existing theme dictionary. The built-in names are thesis, dark, clean, github-light, solarized-light, and one-light. |
| foreground | paint or auto | inherited | Text color for code; auto follows the surrounding text. |
| muted | paint or auto | inherited | Muted text color, including line numbers; auto follows the resolved foreground. |
| fill | auto, paint or none, array of paints or none, or function | inherited | Source-line fill. An array cycles by displayed row; a function receives a row dictionary with index, kind, source-line, and number. |
| accent | paint | inherited | Main accent, including the language badge's default color and (unless explicitly overridden) the first highlight color. |
| stroke | stroke | inherited | Default outline for code elements. |
| radius | length | inherited | Default corner radius. |
| inset | length or dictionary | inherited | Default code-line inset. |
| header-fill, footer-fill, bubble-fill | paint or none | inherited | Backgrounds for the header, footer, and callout bubbles. |
| syntax | auto, str, path, or bytes | inherited | TextMate plist theme for raw-code syntax highlighting. |
| highlight-fill | function | inherited | Callback receiving a highlight color and returning its fill. |
| highlight-colors | paint or nonempty array of paints | inherited | Default highlight color, or a palette cycled by highlights. |
| language-colors | bool | inherited | Whether language badges use their language-specific colors. |
| block, line, number, lang, file, header, footer, highlight, callout, bubble, annotation | dictionary | inherited | Overrides settable fields on the corresponding Codly element. The text entry in a section is a dictionary of native Typst text settings. |

All defaults are inherited from the selected base. Token names and section names are the complete supported top-level keys. Within a section, use fields supported by the corresponding Codly element. The fill callback's row dictionary uses a zero-based displayed-row index; kind is code, skip, or callout, while source-line and number are none for generated rows or numbers that are not displayed.

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Accent also updates the first highlight color.
> If you override accent without supplying highlight-colors, the new accent replaces the first inherited highlight color. An explicit palette takes precedence.

> [!WARNING] Highlight palettes cannot be empty.
> Passing highlight-colors: () causes a compilation error.

The result is a complete dictionary, not a show rule. It starts with the thesis defaults, merges a preset or dictionary base, then merges the named overrides. Section dictionaries merge one level deep, so separate fields such as header: (fill: red) and header: (align: left) can be combined when deriving a theme. Values inside those fields, including callbacks and nested dictionaries, are replaced as complete values.

An unknown preset or top-level key raises an error. Every section override must be a dictionary.

Pass the returned dictionary to [codly.theme](../helpers/theme.md) to render with it. Theme rules are scoped: explicit element fields and later local set rules can override theme values. Section text settings are applied as text settings to text within that element.

 Example: Basic Usage

yaml widgets
- type: select
  name: accent
  label: Accent
  default: 'rgb("ef6c00")'
  options:
    - label: Orange
      value: 'rgb("ef6c00")'
    - label: Blue
      value: 'rgb("1565c0")'
    - label: Green
      value: 'rgb("2e7d32")'

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

let custom = codly.define-theme(
  base: "thesis",
  accent: accent,
  header: (fill: accent.lighten(80%), align: left),
)
show: codly.theme(custom)

codly.new(
  py
  return answer
  ,
  header: [Custom theme],
  highlights: ((line: 1),),
)

title: info
text:
codly.info

Read the source-line count and last displayed line number recorded for a labeled code block.

 Signature

typst code
codly.info(target) -> (last-number: int | none, lines: int)


 Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| target | label | required, positional | Label identifying the code block whose metadata to read. |

The returned dictionary has these fields:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| last-number | int or none | Last computed displayed line number, or none when the block has no numbered source line. |
| lines | int | Number of source lines in the block, including lines omitted from its displayed range. |

 Behavior

> [!WARNING] The target label must identify one code block.
> Labels resolving to zero or multiple locations, or to a location with no later Codly block record, cause a compilation error.

> [!NOTE] lines counts the full source.
> The count includes lines omitted by range; last-number reflects the selected range and offset.

Call [codly.info](signature) inside context, since it queries document content. The helper reads the first Codly block record after the label's location.

Unnumbered rows do not replace last-number. Passing the label as another block's offset adds this number to that block's numbering, so numbering can continue across blocks.

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  
  first
  second
  ,
) 
codly.new(
  
  third
  ,
  offset:  ,
)

  First block: repr(codly.info( ))
]
